### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
Construction resolves the global grid and validates the physical boundary list before `reset` builds layout, outputs,
integrator, coordinates, hydro, scalar, solids and stage buffers.
Options tree supplied by caller; no construction switch.
Order: code map; no independent measured convergence order.
No defining equation: this section maps control flow or data ownership.
:::

Construction resolves the global grid and validates the physical boundary list before `reset` builds layout, outputs,
integrator, coordinates, hydro, scalar, solids and stage buffers. The scalar reconstruction inherits the horizontal
hydro reconstruction when omitted in YAML.

### Derivation

No separate derivation: this section describes an interface or control-flow path. Numerical operators are derived in
their owning chapters.

### Numerical method

The layout exists before boundary classification. Internal slab or cubed faces lose their physical boundary function;
cubed-sphere handling follows its own layout. Output slices must lie in the global half-open bounds and cannot also
request sums on the same axis. Stage registers use float64 with the spatial axes in reverse coordinate order.
Construction does not approximate a differential operator and has no convergence order.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
Layout block count must match partitioning, with the additional panel factor on the cubed sphere. Unsupported output
types, unavailable PnetCDF support and an empty hydro state are rejected at setup. These checks are in the cited
`reset` ranges; no new setup execution is claimed.
:::
